summary: thedata ships an opaque OpenSSL-encrypted blob as its sole export
details: The package's `main` (`index.js`) re-exports `desKey` from `apps/docs/app/theta.js`, which reads `apps/docs/app/des.db` and returns its raw contents. `des.db` is ~49 KB of base64 beginning with `U2FsdGVkX1+`, the OpenSSL `Salted__` header used for AES/DES ciphertext. The rest of the tarball is unrelated Turbo/Next.js scaffolding under a generic name (`thedata`). No code in this package itself decrypts, executes, fetches, or transmits the blob — installing or requiring `thedata` does not on its own read installer secrets, contact a network destination, or run the payload. However, the shape (opaque encrypted blob as the sole meaningful export, wrapped in unrelated scaffolding, generic package name) matches the payload-carrier role in staged supply-chain loader patterns, where a separate compromised package imports `thedata.desKey` and decrypts/executes it.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
